هَلَّابٌ (K) and هَلَّابَةٌ (S, K) A cold wind, with rain. (S, ISd, K.) ―
-b2- يَوْمٌ هَلَّابٌ A day in which is wind and rain: (S:) a day of rain attended by thunder and lightning and terrors, and destructive to dwellings. (IAar.) ―
-b3- Also, A day of gentle, constant, innocuous rain. (IAar.) ―
-b4- Also, A day of dry cold; or dry by reason of cold. (Az, in the T, art. حلب.) ―
-b5- عَامٌ هَلَّابٌ, and ↓ أَهْلَبُ , A year of much rain. (K.) ―
-b6- ↓ عام أَهْلَبُ (tropical:) A plentiful, or fruitful, year; a year of abundant herbage, or vegetation: like أَزَبُّ. (S.) ―
-b7- هَلَّابٌ and ↓ مُهَلِّبٌ and ↓ هَلِيبٌ , (K,) or as in one copy of the K, that of Et-Tabláwee, the last is ↓ هُلَيْبٌ , (TA,) and this is the more correct reading, (MF,) [Three] very cold days, in Kánoon el-'Owwal [or January O. S.]: or in the severe, or intense, cold of winter: (K:) or in the severe, or intense, cold of the month [above mentioned], in the latter part of it. (L.) ＝
-A2- هَلَّابٌ (tropical:) One who satirizes [and reviles] much: (ISh:) [who carps much and severely at others with his tongue: see 1].
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
